name: JSON to TypeScript
blurb: type definitions and a validation schema from sample JSON
intro: Infers types from pasted JSON (one document, an array of samples, or NDJSON) and writes TypeScript interfaces, a Zod schema and a JSON Schema 2020-12. Samples are merged: a key missing from some objects becomes optional, a null makes T | null, and ISO dates, e-mails, UUIDs and URLs get a format.

inputs.label: Sample JSON

{
  "id": "6f1c2d3e-8a4b-4c5d-9e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f",
  "name": "Ada Lovelace",
  "email": "ada@example.com",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-14T09:26:53Z",

examples.title: A user record with nested orders
An NDJSON event log with varying fields

usage: Give json as text (a JSON document, an array of sample objects, or NDJSON), rootName, declare (interface or type), nulls (union or optional) and exportKw. Returns texts 'TypeScript', 'Zod' (v3) and 'JSON Schema' (2020-12), counts of types, fields and optional fields, and a table of the named types. Invalid JSON returns a warning with line and column. Give several samples to learn which fields are optional.
sources: TypeScript Handbook (interfaces, optional properties, union types)
JSON Schema draft 2020-12 core and validation (type, $defs, format)
